title: Shopify Theme Performance — JavaScript, Assets, Liquid & Testing
content: Official Shopify performance best practices (from shopify.dev). Theme Store acceptance requires minimum average Lighthouse performance score of 60 across home, product, and collection pages. JAVASCRIPT: Build themes primarily with HTML and CSS — JavaScript should only serve as progressive enhancement. CSS parses and renders faster than JavaScript. Minified JavaScript bundle size limit: 16 KB or less. Shopify automatically minifies on request. Wrap scripts in IIFE to prevent global namespace collisions. Avoid third-party frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) and large libraries (jQuery). Leverage native browser features and modern DOM APIs. Skip polyfills for browsers lacking async/await. Use defer or async attributes — parser-blocking scripts delay FCP and LCP. RESOURCE LOADING: Add up to two preload resource hints per template (preload_tag filter, preload keyword on stylesheet_tag/image_tag). Use sparingly — only for render-blocking above-fold resources. Lazy-load below-fold images (loading: 'lazy'). Never lazy-load above-fold content. Load non-critical resources on interaction (import-on-interaction pattern). Use system fonts to avoid downloading font resources. ASSET HOSTING: Host on Shopify CDN — avoids unnecessary HTTP connections, enables HTTP/2 prioritisation. Add assets to /assets folder. RESPONSIVE IMAGES: Use image_tag filter which returns srcset with smart default widths (352w, 832w, 1200w, 1920w). Adjust srcset using sizes keyword. Download smallest viable image for device screen. LIQUID: Perform complex operations before loops, not within them. Use Shopify Theme Inspector for Chrome to identify slow code. STYLESHEETS: CSS from {% stylesheet %} tags is automatically subsetted — each page loads only styles from files in its render tree. TESTING: Lighthouse formula: [(product × 31) + (collection × 33) + (home × 13)] / 77. Use median of multiple runs. Use Shopify Lighthouse CI GitHub action for regression detection. Run PageSpeed Insights on mobile and desktop. FIGMA IMPLICATION: When designing, consider performance constraints. Hero images should be optimised for under 200KB. Avoid designs that require heavy JavaScript (complex animations, parallax, infinite scroll). Design with system fonts as a fallback option. Every decorative element you add translates to page weight — be intentional.

title: Shopify Theme Accessibility — WCAG, Keyboard, Colour, Media & Components
content: Official Shopify accessibility best practices (from shopify.dev). Based on WCAG 2.0. Required standard for Theme Store submission. KEYBOARD: Focus indicator visible and consistent. Focus order matches DOM order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). Theme must not rely on mouse hover for visibility/access. Tab/Shift+Tab enable navigation. No sudden context changes on focus. GESTURES: Pinch-to-zoom always available. Complex multi-finger functionality available via single tap/click. PAGE STRUCTURE: Set lang attribute on <html>. Enable viewport zoom — avoid maximum-scale and user-scalable='no'. Include skip link visible on focus. Add tabindex='-1' to main content container. Only use tabindex values 0 or -1. Avoid autofocus. HEADINGS: Semantic h1-h6 in logical sequence. h1 identifies main page topic. NAVIGATION: Wrap with <nav> element. Use aria-current for current page. Avoid role='menu'/role='menuitem' for navigation. DROP-DOWN MENUS: aria-expanded for state, aria-controls for container reference, aria-current for location. Enter/Space opens (focus stays on launcher). Tab moves to first item. Esc collapses and returns focus. PRODUCT INFO: Images include descriptive alt text. Sale/regular prices marked differently visually and with markup. Dynamic price/availability changes communicated via aria-live. CONTROLS: Use <a> for navigation, <button> for actions. Link destination clear from text alone. New window links include warning. FORMS: All fields include labels (aria-label, visually-hidden, floating, or visible). Required inputs have required attribute. Fields use autocomplete. Errors: focus on feedback message, communicated to screen readers, use aria-describedby and aria-live. COLOUR & CONTRAST: Text under 24px regular or 18.5px bold: 4.5:1 ratio. Text 24px+ regular or 18.5px+ bold: 3.0:1. Icons: 3.0:1. Input borders: 3.0:1. Colour must not be sole information indicator. MEDIA: No autoplay. Native HTML controls with toggle states. Space key pauses. All img elements have alt attribute. Decorative images use empty alt=''. Video has closed captions and descriptive audio. TOUCH TARGETS: 44×44px minimum for primary controls and links — main menu links (all levels), form submit buttons, cart and hamburger buttons, modal close buttons, product variant options. DYNAMIC COMPONENTS: Drawers/modals — focus moves to labelling element when opened, keyboard stays within, Esc closes, use role='dialog'. Slideshows — auto-playing content can be paused, content accessible via next/previous buttons. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Check every interactive element is at least 44×44px. Annotate heading levels in your designs (h1, h2, h3). Ensure colour contrast meets ratios — use a Figma contrast checker plugin. Design visible focus states for every interactive element. Design skip-link component. Always include alt text annotations on images in your handoff specs.

title: Shopify Sections & Blocks Best Practices — Modularity, Settings & Metafields
content: Official Shopify best practices for building with sections and blocks (from shopify.dev). Sections and blocks are modular components giving merchants the opportunity to customise and extend their theme. SECTIONS: Available across all pages for template-level customisation. Merchants can add, remove, or reorder content. Control theme settings scoped to entire section layout and content. Static sections cannot be added or removed from Liquid templates or layouts. BLOCKS: Provide granular customisation within sections. Theme settings scoped to individual blocks. Choose block layouts matching content type. Select flexibility levels balancing simplicity with customisation. BLOCK LAYOUTS: Vertical stacking — use for text-based content requiring hierarchy. Horizontal stacking — use when hierarchy is unnecessary. Stack horizontally or create adaptive grids. RESPONSIVE: Allow blocks to wrap across multiple lines or offer sliding controls. Do not squeeze blocks into constrained spaces. LAYOUT INDEPENDENCE: Do not rely on a specific block type or sequence to design a layout. FLEXIBILITY: Group related settings into blocks to reduce complexity rather than creating separate blocks for each attribute. Nest theme settings within blocks. Group elements following specific hierarchies together. ANTI-PATTERN: Creating separate blocks for author, date, and comments instead of grouping them into one blog-meta block. APP BLOCKS: Support app blocks in sections with clear conversion/purchase use cases (product pages, cart templates). Maintain antifragile layouts that resist breaking with unexpected block types. THEME SETTINGS: Provide customisation at section, block, and theme levels. Keep settings to minimum required for majority of merchants. METAFIELDS: Shopify provides standard metafields fitting target segments. Benefits: dynamic content updating contextually, integration with dynamic sources, specialised formatting (electronics specs, coffee origins, care guides). Build specific blocks for metafields. Audit competitor implementations for design opportunities. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design each section with its blocks as a Figma component set. Include variants for different block configurations (e.g. section with 2 blocks, 3 blocks, 4 blocks). Test that sections look good with blocks in any order. Design metafield blocks as generic containers that can hold variable content lengths — never assume fixed text.
